sample_unit: clinical cases (paired discharge reports; 240 reports total)

links.outcome: Expert-rated overall quality of AI-assisted vs physician-written discharge reports on the same cases
links.effect: IAIA achieved a higher overall mean rating than INF (8.14 vs. 7.30 out of 10; p < 0.0001; r ≈ 0.76); superior in 9 of 13 dimensions; non-blinded paired evaluation.
links.quote: IAIA achieved a significantly higher overall mean rating than INF (8.14 vs. 7.30 out of 10; p < 0.0001; r ≈ 0.76, large effect).

links.outcome: Accuracy of allergy and intolerance documentation in AI-generated discharge reports
links.effect: Physician-written reports scored higher on allergies and intolerances (2.69 vs. 2.46; p = 0.002); IAIA tended to use generic formulas.
links.quote: INF retained an advantage only in allergies and intolerances (2.69 vs. 2.46; p = 0.002), where IAIA tended to use generic formulas.

unlisted_practices: Prior local anonymisation of clinical text before generative AI processing (GDPR-oriented architecture)
Sourcing allergy information from verified structured fields or flagging it as pending physician validation

screen.reason: The study retrospectively evaluates the documentary quality of generative AI-drafted discharge summaries compared to physician-written reports across 120 clinical cases, without testing specific deployment safeguard interventions.
